title: ezdwg fixture provenance and bounded AC1015 writer route
mode: Primary-source repository, package, documentation, and corpus-provenance review; plan-only
scope: Resolve the source/license provenance of the named ezdwg ACadSharp sample fixtures.
Reassess ezdwg's current read, write, DWG-to-DXF, and optional interoperability routes.
Refine the existing optional peer gate without adding peer runtimes or fixtures to local fast validation.
Keep explicit 3D entities, ACIS/AcDs carriers, B-rep semantics, and native CAD acceptance separate.

method.kind: Read-only web review of project README, writer guide, named sample-corpus README, PyPI package page, and dwg-rs primary docs
method.limitations: Mutable upstream main pages were reviewed alongside the current PyPI version page. The ezdwg 0.16.3 package was not installed or executed, and package-to-source commit correspondence was not established. ACadSharp fixture origin within ezdwg was resolved only for the five files listed in its nested README; original authoring producers and the provenance of neighboring paired DXFs remain unknown.

sources.revision: Mutable main accessed 2026-10-20; package source mapping not established
sources.observed: The project describes a read-focused Rust-core DWG API for AC1012-AC1032 and a bounded native AC1015 writer. It lists high-level entity coverage but does not provide a complete entity-by-version conformance denominator.
sources.evidence_ceiling: Project-declared API scope; no package runtime or independent format-conformance result.

sources.revision: PyPI package metadata accessed 2026-10-20; release uploaded 2026-10-17
sources.observed: PyPI lists 0.16.3 as the latest release at review time. Earlier plan research identified workspace/lockfile version drift; the package hash does not by itself bind the artifact to the current repository source.
sources.evidence_ceiling: Supports immutable package identification only; no package was installed or run.

sources.project: ezdwg conversion and AC1015 writer guide
sources.observed: The guide limits native DWG writing to AC1015 and enumerates bounded entity, block, and resource support. It excludes ACIS/3DSOLID and complete document metadata, says strict validation covers selected/discovered data, and identifies ezdxf as the DWG-to-DXF writing backend. It documents optional ODA interoperability tests outside ordinary CI.
sources.evidence_ceiling: Implementation-scope and test-design information; no released runtime or ODA acceptance was reproduced.

sources.observed: The nested README names five DWG fixtures, their original paths in the public ACadSharp repository, and the ACadSharp MIT license. It does not state each file's authoring producer or expected-value provenance.
sources.evidence_ceiling: Resolves source repository and stated license for those named files only; does not establish producer independence, paired-DXF provenance, correctness, or permission to copy them into this repository.

sources.observed: The project describes itself as spec-led and pre-alpha, reports per-version decoded/skipped/errored counts, and distinguishes container tests from incomplete per-entity decode coverage.
sources.evidence_ceiling: Potential container-focused comparator only; not a broad semantic oracle or writer-acceptance result.

existingSubplansRefined: PAR-06/PAR-49: bind optional peer evidence to exact artifact, route, version, entity family, and per-source disposition.
PAR-07/S8: do not conflate AC1015 explicit-entity writing, ezdxf-backed DXF projection, ACIS carrier semantics, or native CAD acceptance.
PAR-14: keep all peer runtimes outside per-slice fast validation and continue when external qualification is unavailable.

planChanges: Resolved the stated repository source and MIT license for the five DWGs named under ezdwg/test_dwg/acadsharp, while leaving authoring producer and neighboring paired-DXF provenance unresolved.

Bound the possible ezdwg comparator role to an optional AC1015 explicit-entity question after exact package/source binding; its DWG-to-DXF route is ezdxf-backed and its writer strictness is scoped, not whole-document proof.
Kept peer fixtures out of the repository and required scratch-generated inputs with independently authored expected values.
Made no change to implementation order, validation frequency, peer dependencies, or support claims.
